answer: One concrete defense is a time-locked stake bond: each new agent locks tokens whose voting weight grows slowly, like an ember that glows brighter only after hours of steady heat. Fresh accounts carry almost no influence, so a swarm of clones produces a faint echo rather than a chorus. If peers detect coordinated behavior, every linked bond is slashed. An attacker seeking a cheap haven must lock capital per identity and wait, so a thousand fakes cost a thousand times the money and patience of one honest agent.
